subtitle: As a freelancer I do work in the field of sound design (for all media), producing/mixing of music and programming of (interactive) media installations. Please contact me for more information at me@candidruetter.net.

items.title: Claude Lanzmann. The Recordings
items.role: 3D sound diffusion for tracked headphone system
items.text: The exhibition at the Jüdisches Museum Berlin presents the sound archive of filmmaker Claude Lanzmann, including previously unpublished recordings from his research on the Holocaust. As in Sprachenland, visitors wear headphones tracked in the room, and a binaural engine mixes the sound in real time for each of them. Working for idee und klang, I placed and moved the recordings in 3D space within a digital twin of the exhibition.

links.label: project page at idee und klang

items.title: Zayed National Museum
items.text: The national museum of the United Arab Emirates in Abu Dhabi tells the country's history across six galleries. idee und klang created the sound for the whole museum, more than 100 exhibits including spatial sound installations, media stations and interactive pieces, as well as 27 sounding totems along the paths outside the building. As a freelancer in the team, I worked on the sound design.

links.label: project page at idee und klang

items.title: terminal infinity
items.text: For Alexander Schubert’s multimedia production Terminal Infinity, I designed the video using the 3D software Blender.

items.title: knäuled
items.text: Together with the light collective Göral, we created the audiovisual installation KNÄULED at Neubad in Lucerne. The installation, consisting of 1 km of LED strips, featured a one-hour soundtrack synchronized with the lighting design, with both sound and light influenced by live sensor data.

items.title: Audiobreeze
items.text: For the company Audiobreeze, I programmed a prototype of their immersive 3D audio system, which creates evolving spatial soundscapes from multichannel nature recordings. My work focused on developing and exploring the technical possibilities of the prototype.

items.title: Sprachenland
items.role: 3D sound diffusion for tracked headphone system
items.text: The exhibition Sprachenland at the Landesmuseum Zürich featured a head-tracking system developed by iart, which calculates a real-time binaural 3D mix for each visitor. As a freelancer, I spatialized all the music within a digital twin of the museum.

items.title: HKB Visuelle Kommunikation
items.text: Two series of short animated clips for the Visual Communication programme at the Hochschule der Künste Bern (HKB), made for social media. Each clip answers a question of future students, like “Warum soll ich an der HKB visuelle Kommunikation studieren?” or “Welche Infrastruktur kann ich an der HKB nutzen?”, with hand-drawn animations. I made the sound for all 18 clips.

items.title: asterism
items.text: For the 72-hour performance Asterism at the Maillon Festival in Strasbourg, I spatialized the soundtrack composed by Alexander Schubert to a multichannel setup.

items.title: Schwarm / Fluid
items.text: A generative video and sound installation in two versions for the entrance of KPMG in Zurich. In Schwarm, numbers move through the room like a swarm; their density, spread, speed and position drive the sound synthesis in real time. In Fluid, coloured liquids flow across the screen with a different sound in colour, material and space. Developed at idee und klang with Tweaklab, scenography by LOOSLI & ZEHNDER.

links.label: project page at idee und klang

items.title: Jeu Continu
items.text: A special exhibition about Belle Époque music boxes at the Museum für Musikautomaten in Seewen. Quadraphonic soundscapes in two pavilions contrast the rural Jura villages where the instruments were built with the world exhibitions where they were shown. At headphone stations next to the display cases, visitors hear binaural recordings of restored music boxes from the collection. Realised at idee und klang.

links.label: project page at idee und klang

items.title: Ascend
items.text: A walk-in sound sculpture by Norman Kelley in the lobby of an office building on LaSalle Street, Chicago: a small amphitheatre of steel, brass and marble that works as an instrument. Live data shapes the generative composition: the time of day sets tempo and texture, the day of the week the scale, the weather the timbre. 81 light sensors and 3 motion sensors follow the visitors, and the music plays from the eight nearest of 95 speakers. Sound by idee und klang with iart.

links.label: project page at idee und klang

items.title: Second Layer SoundWalk
items.text: Second Layer SoundWalk is a concept by idee und klang and scenographer Claudia Glass: sound scenography for headphones that adds an interactive, immersive layer to existing exhibitions. My part was the promotional audio piece that presents the idea.
